text: submit publishes queued entries; outside SQPOLL its Zig error-union result counts submissions, not completed operations. submit_and_wait(wait_nr) also requests a completion threshold. With SQPOLL, a successful count from either method may be higher or lower, including zero, than requests actually submitted during that call. The SDK’s submit delegates to submit_and_wait(0); the non-exact SQPOLL rule applies to both. Correlate operation results through CQEs. Do not assume every submit enters the kernel; see Submission queue polling.

fd identifies the ring; to_submit limits SQ entries to consume. min_complete requests a wait threshold with IORING_ENTER_GETEVENTS. Outside SQPOLL, success counts consumed submissions, not successful operations or CQEs copied by the application. With SQPOLL, success generally equals to_submit because the poller submits outside the syscall’s context; it is not an observation of the poller’s actual consumption. Correlate CQEs instead. The syscall does not advance application CQ head. Raw errors are errno-encoded usize values decoded with linux.errno. Operation-specific failures normally arrive separately in CQE res.
